title: gunz 2: the second duel
text: Even with an OP character known as Rena, this game still manages to be quite good. It is a very fast-paced third person shooter with amazing abilities and gameplay. At first, I thought it was going to be just like the mainstream shooters out there. You know, the ones with nothing to do, no abilities to acquire, no blades, and very dull games whose only redeeming factor are the plethora of guns, grenades, and ridiculous camos. This was not the case though. I was thinking, "I might as well try this. If it's♥♥♥♥♥♥then  I will just uninstall the game and be done with it." and decided to try it out. I saw the characters that I could choose from, and noticed that they had cool weapons and looked really cool too. I went with Ivan. As soon as I decided to play the tutorial I realized that this game had more to it than I thought. I was used to most of it, but then the thing that had me sold was the fact that you could run on walls. I had to play it now. I found the campaign to be quite interesting, although not the cinematic story that I prefer. I did like the focus on abilities and design rather than the focus on weapons that most games have. I really enjoy this game and as of typing this, have played 15 hours worth of it. And every single second of those 15 hours were well worth it.

title: half minute hero: super mega neo climax ultimate boy
text: I'd like to start out by stating what may not be obvious at first, Half Minute Hero: Super Mega Neo Climax Ultimate Boy is a combination of the PSP and XBox versions of the game.  If you've played either version, or both then you aren't missing much here.  With that said I this review (like most I suppose) are based entirely on what you believe to be important in a game. The premise of half minute hero is that an evil lord is working a spell to destroy the world, and you have 30 seconds to grind, upgrade your equipment, complete quests and defeat the 'Evil Lord'.  As frantic as it sounds (and can be) you have the Goddess of Time on your side, but as we all know Time is Money, and she will charge you for resetting the clock - while this isn't entirely burdensome it does become expensive quickly which encourages you to move quickly through each quest. The battle system is pretty straight forward requiring very little outside of keeping an eye on your health and using an herb if needed. The PC version has three modes: Hero 30 (which is RPG based), Evil Lord 30 (revolves around summoning minions) and Princess 30 (shooting), plus three unlockable modes (which I honestly haven't unlocked yet). The PC version also includes two graphics modes, retro and 8-bit which was released with the XBox version.  Personally I enjoy the retro look, but that's simply a matter of opinion. The charm and replayability of Half Minute hero is in the humor, multiple branching stories, collectible titles, and equipment.  Although the humor didn't always hit the mark with me, it was still charming in it's own right and although I haven't played through the entire Hero 30 (which is the core game-mode) I did find that collecting titles and unlocking branches could become a little onerous since some of the tasks and hints can be oblique, even with assistance from your caravan. I was initially hesitant to make this purchase because many of the reviews I had read weren't descriptive enough for me (which I hope this fixes for others), but overall I would give this game an 7/10, and dispite it's shortcomings there is more than enough content to justify $9.99, especially if you haven't played the PSP or XBox versions, if you have and you're still interested I would wait until this goes on sale.
